## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi* ("The Second Stage: The Pattern of the Dispensation") is the second chapter of the *Peṭakopadesa* [SuttaCentral]. Secondary studies note that the text analyzes how a disciple's right view of the Buddha's teaching is rooted in two complementary forms of discernment: wisdom arising from what is heard (*sutamayī paññā*), which derives from the phrasing and wording of the doctrines taught, and wisdom arising from reflection (*cintāmayī paññā*), which develops through inward appropriate attention to their essential meaning [Gal 2003; Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics].
According to SuttaCentral, passage-level parallels are found in the following chapter of the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 3) as well as the *Puggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.1); the text also shares doctrinal verses and motifs with the *Mahāpadāna Sutta* (DN 14), *Dhammapada* verses (Dhp 1, Dhp 183), and extensive parallel verses preserved in Gāndhārī, Patna, Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese Dharmapada and Udānavarga collections [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal text reuse across 172 texts, highlighted by an extensive overlap with its counterpart section in the *Nettippakaraṇa*, the *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna* (Ne 37; 250 shared passages), confirming the relationship noted by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Further text reuse occurs in Nettippakaraṇa commentaries (*Nettivibhāvinī* and *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*), other parts of the *Peṭakopadesa* (such as Pe 8), and canonical discourses across the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 4, AN 5, AN 6, AN 9, AN 10), *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 22, SN 40, SN 55), and the *Udāna* (Ud 3.10) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali literature, DharmaNexus detects cross-language alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan collections, including Tibetan and Sanskrit versions of the *Udānavarga*, Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha*, the *Mahāvastu-avadāna*, and the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
